question: Should OpenClaw publish official standalone Android APKs outside Google Play, and which signed flavor, release channel, provenance process, and support policy should own that distribution?
rationale: Current code can archive a signed third-party APK locally, but making it an official GitHub Release or F-Droid asset changes release trust, sideload guidance, signing custody, and support expectations.

options.title: Approve signed standalone APK releases
options.body: Reuse or harden the existing third-party APK archive path, publish checksums/provenance with release assets, and update Android docs for non-Play installs.

options.title: Stay Google Play-only
options.body: Keep official Android distribution on Google Play and update docs to state that standalone APKs are not currently published or supported.

options.title: Prefer F-Droid or vetted channel first
options.body: Investigate F-Droid or another vetted distribution channel before GitHub APK assets, with the same signing and provenance requirements.

recommendation.title: Approve signed standalone APK releases
recommendation.body: Reuse or harden the existing third-party APK archive path, publish checksums/provenance with release assets, and update Android docs for non-Play installs.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Android product direction, release trust, and user-facing docs, and the Android app/release history points most strongly to steipete for that cross-cutting call.
